notes: The window layer. The browser page is the window, so there is no window manager: CreateWindowExA reports the client rectangle it was given, and the frame loop is a PeekMessageA loop that draws when the queue is empty.

functions.name: RegisterClassA
functions.description: The class only has to be remembered so CreateWindowExA can find its window procedure. The atom is a stable non-zero index, not a real atom table entry.
functions.evidence: trace: one registration before the only window is created

functions.name: CreateWindowExA
functions.description: The one window the game draws into. All four coordinates arrive as CW_USEDEFAULT, so the host substitutes the 640x480 surface instead of asking the OS.
functions.evidence: trace: called once with CW_USEDEFAULT for x, y, width and height

functions.name: ShowWindow
functions.description: The page is visible whenever the guest runs, so this is where the activation messages are queued exactly once: WM_ACTIVATE, WM_SETFOCUS, WM_ACTIVATEAPP. Posting them on every call would make the game re-initialise its input each frame.
functions.evidence: trace: called once from WinMain, immediately followed by the message loop

functions.name: PeekMessageA
functions.description: Zero means "no message", and that is what makes the frame loop draw: the guest only paints when the queue is empty, exactly as it did on Windows with no input arriving.
functions.evidence: trace: 30-60 calls per second, one per frame, in every screen

functions.name: GetMessageA
functions.description: Cannot block, because the page cannot interrupt a host call and a real block would freeze the tab. An empty queue is answered with WM_NULL rather than WM_QUIT, so the guest keeps running long enough for the next event.
functions.evidence: trace: reached only on the dialog paths; returning WM_QUIT there ended the process immediately

functions.name: DispatchMessageA
functions.description: Hands the message to the window procedure the class registered, through the session's guest-call mechanism. The import finishes with that procedure's return value, so the guest sees a normal dispatch.
functions.evidence: trace: window procedure at 0x00457da3 receives WM_KEYDOWN from this path

functions.name: AdjustWindowRectEx
functions.description: Leaves the rectangle untouched: the rehost has no border and no title bar, so the client rectangle is already the window rectangle.
functions.evidence: trace: called once before CreateWindowExA; the game never re-reads the result

functions.name: GetAsyncKeyState
functions.description: Bit 15 is the key's state now, bit 0 whether it was pressed since the last read, and that second bit is consumed by the read as on Windows. Losing the consume makes a single tap repeat forever.
functions.evidence: trace: polled every frame by the game's own key handling, not through the message queue

functions.name: ShowCursor

stub.body:
host.windows.cursor_visible += if call.arg(0)? != 0 { 1 } else { -1 };
    Ok(Return(host.windows.cursor_visible as u32))

functions.description: Windows keeps a display counter that hides the pointer at zero. Keeping the same arithmetic means the game's ShowCursor(FALSE) hides the page's own pointer instead of doing nothing.
functions.evidence: trace: balanced pairs around the play screens, unbalanced around the menus

functions.name: SystemParametersInfoA
functions.description: SPI_GETWORKAREA is answered with the surface rect (no taskbar, no other windows). Anything else is refused with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER rather than writing zeroes the game would act on.
functions.evidence: trace: only SPI_GETWORKAREA is requested, once, to centre the window

functions.name: ReleaseDC
functions.description: Device contexts here are numbers with no resource behind them, so releasing always succeeds.
functions.evidence: trace: paired with GetDC in the same routine
